transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (NeuroScale ML Lead), Carlos Mendes (NeuroScale SRE), Jasmine Lee (Product)

Summary:
Quick sync to review last week's quantization runs (INT8 and FP8), compare quality deltas, discuss perf numbers, and agree next steps for pilot expansion. Some noisy transcription; some terms mis-heard.

Topics:
- INT8 baseline runs on 4xA100 and p4d-like infra
- FP8 experimental runs and stability concerns
- Quality metrics: n-gram/semantics, human eval notes, edge-case failures
- Throughput & latency deltas, memory footprint reductions
- Risk/rollback plan and security/integration questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood, elena and I will lead. quick agenda, run through numbers then next steps
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, uh we, we ran the INT8 set last night on the 8k eval, results came through, I'm keen to see the delta versus fp32
[00:31] Elena: cool i'll walk through the spreadsheet, FYI there are two tabs, the "8k-main" and the "edge-case". link is in the notes, drive.google.com/spreadsheets/quant-bench (shared)
[00:45] Carlos: small note, our SRE ran into OOM on the smaller host when we tried the fp8 experimental build, so we pulled that one off to a bigger instance
[01:02] Samir: yeah we saw that, fp8 has a different memory profile, sometimes higher peak mem due to pack/unpack ops, that's expected, elena do you want to call out the INT8 numbers?
[01:17] Elena: sure. so INT8 average latency per token dropped by ~20% on our p4d-equivalent instance, throughput improved roughly 1.7x on streaming workloads. quality-wise, automatic metrics show a 0.8% drop on the semantic-sim score and approx 1.2% drop on exact-match for the instruction-following subset
[01:39] Priya: hmm 1.2% is within noise for most of our flows, but we care about that 0.8% on long-form summarization, we saw some hallucinations in 3 of the 500 samples
[01:55] Elena: right, we flagged those. important to note, INT8 used per-channel quantization with a small calibration set; we didn't run advanced layerwise kl yet which may recover some quality
[02:10] Samir: good point, calibration tune could recover. fp8—what did that show?
[02:18] Elena: FP8 gave us higher throughput — about 2.2x in steady-state — and latency drop around 28%, but quality varied. on the same 8k eval we saw a 3.3% drop on the semantic metric and 2.9% exact-match drop. also more variance across prompts
[02:38] Jasmine: sorry can I ask, is that variance mostly on math/qa style prompts or on generation length?
[02:46] Elena: mostly creative/generative long-form and some math/chain-of-thought where numeric stability matters. short instructions and classification style prompts mostly fine
[02:56] Carlos: the OOM we hit was when fp8 was packing kv cache differently on smaller GPUs; larger mem solved it but we'll need guidance for mem footprint in dedicated pool
[03:12] Samir: action there, elena will run a memory profile and recommend min instance sizes, we'll include buffer for kv packing.
[03:27] Priya: on quality, we also had human raters look at a 200-sample slice for fp8 and they gave an average acceptability 92% versus 96% for fp32. so that's a 4 point drop, which aligns with the metric numbers
[03:45] Elena: ai-generated transcripts sometimes swap names — the sheet has the raw scores and the normalized sem-sim. we also added a per-prompt failure tag so you can sort by failure mode
[03:58] Samir: great. do we have any quick insight into prompt categories where INT8 fails vs FP8 fails?
[04:08] Elena: INT8 failures are concentrated on out-of-distribution token distributions and very long context with repeated patterns — that's kv mis-scaling. FP8 failures skew to numeric stability and rare tokens; it is more brittle on step-by-step math
[04:29] Priya: interesting. can we try mixed-mode — INT8 for base layers, fp16/FP8 for attention or math-sensitive layers? any config support for that?
[04:39] Elena: yes we support mixed-precision profiles, we didn't enable that for the reported runs to keep apples-to-apples. next run we can try an attention-preserve profile: quantize feedforward to INT8 and keep attention in FP16/FP8 hybrid
[04:54] Samir: good plan. also, question from compliance side — we need to confirm KMS integration for the private pilot and key rotation, samir can you send the security doc?
[05:07] Samir: yes i'll attach the KMS/KMS note, and certs, and SOC2 docs to the thread after the call
[05:15] Jasmine: thanks, please include SSO/SAML checklist and the admin RBAC page, we need to show that to legal
[05:22] Samir: will do.
[05:28] Carlos: one more infra note, can you share the network egress profile for dedicated pools? our security team needs estimated CIDR ranges and egress ports
[05:38] Elena: i'll add a network appendix to the benchmark doc and include minimal firewall/egress rules
[05:44] Samir: back to perf — elena, any variance by sequence length?
[05:49] Elena: yes, throughput gains are most pronounced at medium sequence lengths (512-2048 tokens) because batching is more efficient, for ultra-long sequences the kv packing overhead reduces gains, so perf delta shrinks to ~1.2x for >8k contexts
[06:06] Priya: that's relevant because our summarization sometimes goes to 10k, so we need to see those real-world runs
[06:12] Samir: we can run the 10k slice as part of the next pass, include both INT8 and FP8. we'll also add the customer-provided edge prompts
[06:21] Priya: perfect. on the user-experience side, how transparent is model variant routing? we want fallback to fp32 on failure or high-uncertainty responses
[06:31] Elena: Redwood runtime supports routing policies — you can set per-route thresholds and automatic fallback to a safety variant (fp32) if the model emits low confidence or if certain hallucination heuristics trigger
[06:44] Jasmine: can that be per-endpoint? like only on the summarization endpoint not for embeddings or classification?
[06:50] Elena: yes per-route configurations are supported, and we can show a demo of the rollback/canary flow in the console
[06:58] Samir: next on the timeline, do we have agreement to run the dedicated benchmark after Samir's FP8 stability run?
[07:06] Priya: yes we are ok to proceed, assuming we get the security docs and the mem-profile guidance
[07:12] Carlos: we also need a short SLA-like doc for the pilot (uptime and latency SLO) to map expectations for the dedicated pool
[07:20] Samir: we'll draft a pilot SLO one-pager and share, shouldn't be heavy.
[07:26] Elena: one more technical note — quantization checkpointing: when we apply per-layer calibration it increases the build time for the compiled kernel by ~15-20%, so there's a tradeoff on deployment lead time vs quality
[07:40] Priya: okay understood, we'll weigh that. for go/no-go, our product team wants to keep quality delta under 2% semantic-sim and <2% exact-match for core flows
[07:52] Jasmine: and business wants at least 1.5x cost reduction to make moving off hosted worthwhile
[07:58] Samir: that gives clear targets.
[08:02] Elena: final housekeeping — the sheet includes a col for "customer-impact" where we mark regressions as blocker/ok/minor, please review and flag anything you think is miscategorized
[08:15] Priya: will do.
[08:18] Samir: recap of action items and owners, we'll follow up and schedule the dedicated run, thanks everyone
[08:25] Carlos: thanks all
[08:28] (call ends)
